title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Matchday Board for the Command Centre redesign. Lock it, take the pick or an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Matchday Board
options.lineage: football fixture boards, team sheets and league tables
options.thesis: Every item is a pick: what is on the team sheet today, what kicks off when, and where the table stands.
options.viewport: Masthead as the team-sheet header with dateline and kickoff line; below it the selection — today's items needing a decision, first action above the fold; the right rail lists this week's fixtures with kickoff times; KPI progress runs beneath as a ruled league table with form guide.
options.risk: Football words leaking into product copy would turn structure into costume; terminology stays RIL's.

raised.raise: Colour is the sheet, never the mark — RIL blue appears only as whole committed fields, never as tinted icons or accents.
Stable row codes — every item carries a visible number so it can be called out by code, not just seen.
Margin number rail — one strict ruled margin column indexes every row on the board.
Leader-line annotations — counts are pinned to the rows they measure with hairline leaders, not floated in cards.

regions.label: fixture rail: this week's kickoff times

options.label: The Flatplan
options.lineage: magazine flat plans and issues grids
options.thesis: The whole month as one ruled grid of cells, each piece of content carrying its own state.
options.viewport: One full-width plan grid where each cell is a ruled rectangle holding a status word, code and date; decision cells flag at the top-left; a thin masthead above; counts printed in the grid's gutter rather than in cards.
options.risk: Familiar: a planning grid is one step from the KPI-card dashboard this redesign refuses — cells must read as printed plan, never as tiles.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.thesis: The workspace as a broadcast index: numbered pages, fixed status colours, keyboard first.
options.viewport: A 40 by 24 character lattice: section header row, numbered page rows for each queue, a status panel keyed by three-digit codes.
options.risk: Retro-novelty if the cell discipline slips even slightly.
options.case: Holds clarity — a rigid lattice, explicit status vocabulary and direct page addressing serve scanning; loses identification, since fixture boards are everyday objects and teletext is not.

options.label: Destination Blind
options.lineage: depot destination blinds and cloth roll displays
options.thesis: The queue as cloth courses stepping under one fixed window; a fault stops a row mid-step.
options.viewport: One fixed window inset from the trim with queued courses stepping beneath it in whole line-heights; a punched eyelet tape down the edge as the index.
options.risk: One window hides as much as it shows; on a dense morning queue that can cost a scan.
options.case: Holds clarity — stepped whole-row motion and a mid-row fault seam are strong queue states; loses identification, since transit cloth is not a marketing team's daily object.

options.label: Event Catalog Grid
options.lineage: convention circle catalogs printed on newsprint
options.thesis: Every item a postage-stamp cell in a numbered hall grid, circled in pen when picked.
options.viewport: Thousands of tiny cells packed edge to edge, each with a code; picked cells circled by hand, visited ones struck through.
options.risk: A grid of stamps needs imagery the workspace does not have.
options.case: Loses both: niche print culture most marketing teams do not know, and thumbnail cells need pictures the queues do not carry.
options.kept: Stable numbered addressing — every row call-able by code.

options.label: Copy-Shop Zine
options.thesis: One typed column on coloured stock; display type enlarged until the counters fill.
options.viewport: A single 65-character typed column running the full sheet, with one heading blown up until it runs off the edge.
options.risk: One column cannot hold a triage board.
options.case: Loses both: a single typed column cannot carry queue, schedule and table at once; print-shop colour is not this audience's daily object.
options.kept: Colour is the sheet, never the mark — colour appears only as whole committed fields.

options.label: Fold Sequence
options.thesis: One uncut sheet passing through thirty-two numbered, discrete states.
options.viewport: A strict margin column of fold numbers beside square diagrams of one sheet at successive authored states.
options.risk: A fold sequence is one object, not a queue.
options.case: Loses both: no natural home for parallel queues or schedules, and the crane is not this audience's object.
options.kept: A strict margin rail of numbers indexing every row.

options.label: Force Diagram
options.thesis: Metrics as a network of tension and compression with values pinned to nodes.
options.viewport: A strut network with annotated counts on leader lines and force values in monospaced labels.
options.risk: A force diagram belongs to engineering, not to a morning triage.
options.case: Loses both: no structure for queues, schedule or approvals, and engineering mechanics is foreign to this audience.
options.kept: Hairline leader lines pinning each value to the row it measures.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The SaaS overview executed impeccably: sidebar, four KPI cards, a chart row, a table.
canonCard.viewport: Left nav, a four-up KPI card row, two chart cards, and a data table below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every competitor's dashboard by design.
